text:
Mira: Heads up — running into weirdness with canary routing when we combine header-based overrides and cookie stickiness. Some sessions are landing 100% on canary.
Sam: Oof. Can you paste the route config? header overrides should take precedence, but stickiness can reassign buckets.
Mira: Here's the rule snippet:
```
route:
  match: path_prefix("/v1/generate")
  canary:
    weight: 5
    header_override: "x-canary=true"
    cookie_name: "rw_canary"
```
Mira: When a user has rw_canary=canary and later sets x-canary=true, we expect canary -> still 100% is wrong for many.
Vikram: I suspect the bucket computation happens before header override and we then honor cookie after override. There was a change to bucket sharding last month.
Anya: Console telemetry shows canary nodes spiking in CPU for a ~30m window at 02:10 UTC — matches the thread. A bunch of requests had both header and cookie present.
Sam: Repro: send header + existing cookie; I see the router sets sticky assignment then reapplies header override logic, but due to a short-circuit bug it never clears the sticky bucket leading to reassigning traffic.
Mira: Any quick mitigations? Want to avoid reverting the whole canary rollout.
Vikram: Short term: prefer header override by ensuring header match happens after cookie check and if header present, set response cookie to reflect header assignment (so subsequent requests are consistent). That requires small runtime tweak.
Anya: Also adding metric: canary_assignments_by_reason { reason: header|cookie|bucket } so console rollout UX can break down traffic source.
SRE Oncall: If canary nodes are overloaded we should abort auto-rollout. Can we add a guard in the rollout flow to check node CPU > 65% and pause? quick fix in the control plane.
Sam: I'll open a PR to change precedence + emit the new metric. Also adding an opt-in flag in rollout UI: "preserve-cookie-on-header-override" so customers pick behavior.
Deploy Bot: deploy scheduled: canary-router-fix -> staging at 1763366400
Mira: Thanks — please tag me on the PR and add a dashboard panel for canary_assignments_by_reason. :thumbsup:
